scope: Product architecture/model/license research only. No fullweights,modelinference,appchanges orWindowsperformanceverification.

products.name: Superwhisper
findings: Ships S1-mini on macOS and Windows x64; full offline processing also requires a local voice model.
English Message and Mail modes only. Default S1-Language and broader mode selections can be cloud.
462 MB is listed model size. Speed10 is a relative rating; the public measured benchmark covers speech models.
products.model_reuse_status: Consult the separate S1-mini license audit before bundling.

products.name: Dikt
findings: Official guide documents local Whisper followed by S1-mini in Windows Local-Only mode.
Guide lists a 462 MB download and approximately 600 MB active cleanup RAM; it provides no matched whole-app latency distribution.
Optional cloud AI cleanup runs after local cleanup and sends the resulting text to its provider.
products.model_reuse_status: Independent S1-mini deployment evidence; same model terms apply.

products.name: Spokenly
findings: Ships a task-trained Qwen3-0.6B-Base fine-tune with rank 32 all-layer LoRA, greedy decoding and a 4096-token prompt-plus-answer training window.
Windows/Linux use Q8_0 GGUF and llama.cpp. Mac uses fixed-window Core ML on the Neural Engine; macOS15 uses a shorter CPU/Float32 path.
Special key:value prompt ends in out:; only text is required. Six languages beyond English have lower stated quality.
Publisher reports approximately 120 tokens/s on Core i5-12400F,0.3 s short cleanup and 650 MB model-loaded RAM; long inputs take seconds and more memory. These are not our measurements.
products.model_reuse_status: Apache-2.0 text and notices retrieved at immutable revisions; concrete reusable model lead.

publisher_performance.scope: publisher model-only statements; not our measurement

products.name: Whisperstream
findings: Actual source identifies its own Stream-1 Mini fine-tune, distinct from Superwhisper S1-mini.
Default English Chat/Email artifact is 484,215,648 bytes at a pinned revision. Gemma E2B is a separate Customizable option.
llama-server uses bounded4096-token context, preparation during recording, resident workers and idle offload. Each model must pass a per-machine speed check.
products.model_reuse_status: Consult the specialist model audit; application source is GPL-3.0-only and model terms are separate.

products.name: VoiceInk / Refine V1
findings: Source ships Refine V1, a Qwen3.5-2B task fine-tune with affine4-bit/group 64 weights; weight artifact is 1,059,404,951 bytes.
MLX GPU inference disables thinking, warms before cleanup, clears request sessions and uses a separate XPC worker with 10-second idle grace.
64 MiB is an allocator-cache limit, not total model memory. Availability requires Apple silicon and 16 GiB physical memory.
products.model_reuse_status: Restricted: license prohibits commercial use, redistribution and use in other software or open-source projects without permission. Architecture reference only.

products.name: Quobi (voice-type paths) / Quill
findings: CPU Parakeet ASR is followed by Quill cleanup through llama.cpp Vulkan, with CPU fallback.
Quill comprises task-trained Qwen3.5-derived0.8B,2B and 4B models with distinct cleanup modes.
Approximate extra-second cleanup is a publisher product claim without a matched workload distribution. Existing Freehand Quill4B failures remain relevant.
products.model_reuse_status: Base Quill models are Apache-2.0; application is AGPL-3.0 with a commercial licensing option.

products.name: Muesli
findings: Actual managed catalog pins task-trained Qwen0.8B/2B, LFM1.2B and Gemma E2B variants.
Qwen0.8B Q4 is 529,296,832 bytes;2B Q4 is 1,274,396,096 bytes; LFM Q4 is 730,898,432 bytes; Gemma LiteRT is 2,946,098,832 bytes.
Source includes GGUF/MLX paths and a LiteRT Gemma artifact with an MTP head. Resolve abbreviated revisions to complete commits before acquisition.
products.model_reuse_status: Application is MIT. Qwen/Gemma and LFM derivative terms require separate model audits.

products.name: Handy
cleanup_models: User-selected local model through OpenAI-compatible endpoint
findings: Local ASR and optional text postprocessing are separate. Postprocessing is disabled by default.
Source includes Apple Intelligence on macOS ARM64 and a custom OpenAI-compatible provider defaulting to localhost:11434/v1.
Default provider is OpenAI when postprocessing is enabled without another choice. No bundled task-trained cleanup weights were established.
products.model_reuse_status: Application MIT; local server and selected model terms remain independent.

products.name: OpenWhispr
findings: Actual local llama.cpp integration and a 42-model catalog provide general-model discovery leads.
Catalog includes LFM2.5 230M Q8 at 246.6 MB,350M Q8 at 379.2 MB,1.2B Q4 at 730.9 MB and Qwen3.5-0.8B Q4 at 579.6 MB.
GPU selection, context sizing and thinking suppression are implemented; catalog adjectives and recommendation flags do not prove fidelity.
products.model_reuse_status: Application MIT; inspect each upstream model license, particularly Liquid terms.

products.name: MacWhisper
findings: Official support distinguishes AI provider selection from speech model selection.
Apple on-device Foundation Models, Ollama and LM Studio can process transcript text locally; hosted AI services send transcript text remotely.
External servers must remain running and count toward complete-pipeline resource measurements. No distinct bundled specialist model was established.
products.model_reuse_status: Proprietary application; platform and user-selected model licenses are independent.

products.name: Voicetypr (ideaplexa)
cleanup_models: S1-mini and trainedLFM350 are plan-only leads
findings: Actual source supports custom-endpoint AI polish, output guards, protected terms and a conservative no-op detector for clean short text.
S1-mini integration and a trained350M model are discussed in a future plan, not established as a shipped native model by inspected source.
Plan056 explicitly leaves exact S1-mini license wording unresolved and says not to bundle until resolved.
products.model_reuse_status: Application AGPL-3.0; endpoint model terms independent. Do not treat a plan as deployment or permission.

products.name: TypeWhisper
findings: Windows local text plugin uses LLamaSharp CPU; Mac plugins use MLX or llama.cpp Metal.
Fixed catalog starts at Qwen3.5-2B Q4 around 1.3 GB; larger Gemma and LFM choices plus custom GGUF imports are supported.
Explicit load/unload and cached verification are implemented. LFM2.5-2.6B always reasons and source warns of several-second responses.
products.model_reuse_status: Application GPL/commercial options; Qwen/Gemma Apache declarations, Liquid custom terms and runtime MIT remain separate.

products.name: FluidVoice / Fluid Intelligence
findings: Optional Fluid Intelligence is local, but its runtime is privately maintained.
Public provider boundary names Pico/Mini hardware tiers; base-model identity and reusable weight license were not established.
Hardware selection uses memory and GPU bandwidth heuristics, explicitly without a latency guarantee. Avoid the unaffiliated fluidvoice.org domain.
products.model_reuse_status: Core application GPLv3; private runtime/model is architecture-only evidence for this inventory.

products.name: WhisperLocal (usingcolor)
findings: Actual on-device choices are Apple SystemLanguageModel and optional Gemma4 E2B through MLX, after filler stripping.
Published125-case scripted benchmark reports substantial hard failures; one author, one judge and one run per case limit generalization.
Its four OSS benchmark challengers are not shipped providers. No universal650 MB/700 ms claim follows.
products.model_reuse_status: Application MIT; Gemma Apache terms separate, Apple system API is not redistributable Windows weights.

products.name: Scribe
findings: Actual Windows product supports Ollama, LM Studio, TensorSharp and Foundry Local.
Published benchmark uses RTX5080 16 GB, Ryzen9 9900X and 95 GB RAM;25 difficult dictations and AI judge scores.
Gemma E2B cleanup median/p95 is 327/532 ms on GPU; CPU examples are2.4–3.3 s. The measurements exclude ASR and delivery.
Techniques include static prompt prefixes, mentioned vocabulary, GPU residency and optional MTP speculation.
products.model_reuse_status: Source/runtime/model terms need individual review; no new exclusive small specialist weights established.

products.name: Winpepper
findings: Actual Windows source uses in-process LLamaSharp cleanup after ASR; default Qwen2.5-0.5B Q4 is 491,400,032 bytes.
Additional catalog entries include LFM1.2B, Granite1B and manual Sotto350M Q8 conversion, with model-specific prompt handling.
Source records an LFM worked-example echo problem; removing the example improved that particular test. Readme acknowledges several-second cleanup on weak hardware.
products.model_reuse_status: Review each upstream license. Sotto MIT wording in a source comment does not replace review of underlying Liquid terms.

products.name: Whispering / Epicenter
findings: Current app uses user-authored transformations and a saved text endpoint; none runs until configured.
Requests send transformation instructions and transcript text to the selected local or remote endpoint. Local file storage is independent of inference locality.
A historic migration ADR is not proof of a currently bundled specialist model.
products.model_reuse_status: Application/source and external model licenses remain separate.

products.name: Pomvox cleanup engine SDK
findings: Inspectable public-beta Swift SDK supports MLX prefix preparation and prompt-lookup speculative verification, with explicit queue/deadline/fallback outcomes.
Pinned Simplewords8-bit weight artifact is approximately 2 GB and access is gated. Pack model ID and license URL use different repository names.
README explicitly labels sub100 ms cleanup as a target, not a measured capability. M1 16 GiB is tested; Windows/Linux inference is not supported in this milestone.
products.model_reuse_status: Core SDK MIT. Pack Apache label is not a full upstream model-license/access audit.

products.name: Windows Voice Access + Fluid dictation
findings: Microsoft documents offline Voice Access ASR plus on-device Phi Silica grammar/punctuation/filler refinement on eligible Copilot+ PCs.
Copilot+ eligibility requires 40+ NPU TOPS. Intel officially lists Core Ultra7 155H at 11 NPU TOPS.
No inspected source establishes the same complete-app RAM and release-to-delivery budget or full spoken-correction fidelity.
products.model_reuse_status: Closed platform feature/API, not redistributable GGUF weights.

products.name: Windows Win+H Voice Typing + Fluid dictation
findings: Microsoft documents local Phi Silica refinement in Win+H, but voice typing itself still uses Azure online speech recognition.
This is a hybrid flow; Voice Access is the separate offline speech path.
products.model_reuse_status: Closed platform feature; not a fully local pipeline.

source_capture.website_evidence: Webtool text extraction snapshots; not rawHTML, notimmutablepublisherrefs. URLandcapturetimepreserved.
source_capture.performance: All new external performance figures are publisher-reported, not independently rerun.

limitations: No inspected product establishes both 650 MB total host RAM and 700 ms complete delivery on matched target-hardware trials.
Short-input latency cannot be extended to long paragraphs.
Cleanup weight-file size is not whole-app RAM.
Report prefix-cache state, GPU/CPU choice, work during recording and fallback/bypass coverage separately.
Local ASR or local history storage does not prove local enhancement.
